entries.clue: Core body temperature drop below normal range, a common perioperative risk
entries.rationale: The nurse applies warmed blankets and monitors temperature closely to prevent this in the recovery room.

entries.clue: The body's process of stopping bleeding through vasoconstriction and clot formation
entries.rationale: The nurse applies direct pressure to support this process when a patient has active external bleeding.

entries.clue: Removal of an artificial airway once a patient can breathe independently
entries.rationale: The nurse assesses gag reflex and oxygen saturation closely in the minutes following this procedure.

entries.clue: Rapid swelling of the deeper layers of skin, often affecting the face or airway
entries.rationale: The nurse treats swelling near the lips or tongue from this reaction as a potential airway emergency.

entries.clue: Painful inflammation and ulceration of mucous membranes, often from chemotherapy
entries.rationale: The nurse recommends frequent gentle oral care to help manage discomfort from this condition.

entries.clue: Rigid device applied to immobilize a fractured limb during healing
entries.rationale: The nurse checks circulation, movement, and sensation distal to this device to catch compartment syndrome early.

entries.clue: Muscle or tendon injury caused by overstretching or overuse
entries.rationale: The nurse distinguishes this from a ligament injury when teaching a patient about musculoskeletal pain.

entries.clue: Placement of a tube into the trachea to secure and maintain an airway
entries.rationale: The nurse gathers suction and confirms tube placement with capnography immediately after this procedure.

entries.clue: Allergic skin reaction producing raised, itchy welts
entries.rationale: The nurse assesses for this skin finding as an early sign of an allergic or anaphylactic reaction.

entries.clue: Relief from pain, typically achieved with medication
entries.rationale: The nurse reassesses pain level after administering this to confirm the intervention was effective.

entries.clue: Preoperative order meaning the patient may have nothing by mouth
entries.rationale: The nurse verifies this status before surgery to reduce the risk of aspiration during anesthesia.

entries.clue: Steady pulling force applied to a limb to align or immobilize a fracture
entries.rationale: The nurse ensures weights hang freely and are never removed without a provider's order during this therapy.

entries.clue: Surgical cut made to access underlying tissue
entries.rationale: The nurse inspects this site for redness, warmth, or drainage as signs of postoperative infection.

entries.clue: Profound involuntary weight loss and muscle wasting seen in advanced cancer or chronic illness
entries.rationale: The nurse assesses nutritional intake and albumin levels when this wasting syndrome is suspected.

entries.clue: Medically induced state of reduced consciousness used to ease anxiety before a procedure
entries.rationale: The nurse monitors airway patency and oxygen saturation continuously while a patient is in this state.

entries.clue: Absence of disease-causing microorganisms maintained through sterile technique
entries.rationale: The nurse maintains this principle throughout a sterile dressing change to prevent surgical site infection.

entries.clue: Ligament injury caused by a sudden twist or wrench of a joint
entries.rationale: The nurse teaches RICE therapy (rest, ice, compression, elevation) for this common soft-tissue injury.

entries.clue: Rigid or flexible device used to immobilize and support an injured body part
entries.rationale: The nurse applies this before transport to prevent further tissue damage from an unstable fracture.

entries.clue: Class of analgesic whose major adverse effect is respiratory depression
entries.rationale: The nurse keeps naloxone available and monitors respiratory rate closely whenever this class of drug is given.
